learningObjectives: Use hardware button and orientation Modules to simulate physical device interaction.
Automate biometric prompts on Android and iOS, including the Perfecto-specific biometrics Modules.
Move files on and off the device and manage Appium session lifecycle explicitly.
Apply a systematic troubleshooting checklist to mobile automation failures.

elements.title: Simulating physical device controls
items: ME3.0 Hardware Button Operations — simulates physical buttons: Home, Back (Android), volume, and power, for flows that depend on hardware-level interaction rather than an on-screen control.
ME3.0 Set Device Orientation — rotates the device between portrait and landscape, for apps or screens whose layout or behaviour changes with orientation.

bulletPoints: Hardware Button Operations = simulate physical buttons (Home/Back/volume/power).
Set Device Orientation = rotate portrait/landscape for orientation-dependent flows.

elements.title: Biometric automation Modules
items: Use Android fingerprint authentication — simulates a fingerprint match against an Android biometric prompt.
Use iOS biometric authentication — simulates Face ID / Touch ID matching an iOS biometric prompt.
Set iOS biometrics enrollment — configures whether the simulated device/simulator is treated as having biometrics enrolled at all, a prerequisite before the authentication Module can succeed.

Use Perfecto biometrics authentication / Handle Perfecto Image Injection — biometrics and camera-input simulation specific to devices hosted on the Perfecto cloud device lab, for teams whose device farm is Perfecto-backed rather than local/USB.

elements.text: Enrollment state and authentication are separate steps on iOS — a biometric authentication Module will not succeed against a simulator that hasn't first been configured as enrolled via Set iOS biometrics enrollment.

bulletPoints: Android and iOS each have their own biometric Modules — they are not interchangeable.
On iOS: enrollment must be set before authentication can be simulated.
Perfecto-specific Modules exist for teams using the Perfecto cloud device lab rather than local devices.

elements.title: Moving data and managing sessions
items: Upload File to Mobile Device / Download File from Mobile Device — moves files between the automation host and the device's filesystem, useful for seeding test data or retrieving generated output (e.g. an exported PDF or report) for verification.
Get Appium Session Id — retrieves the underlying session identifier, useful when correlating Tosca execution against raw Appium/TMA logs during troubleshooting.
End Appium Session — explicitly closes the session rather than relying on it to time out, freeing the device for the next TestCase or the next person in a shared device-farm setting.

bulletPoints: Upload/Download File Modules move data between host and device filesystem.
Get Appium Session Id helps correlate Tosca-level failures with raw driver logs.
End Appium Session explicitly frees a shared device rather than waiting on a timeout.

elements.term: A dedicated Module for a transient component
elements.description: Android Snackbar steers the Android Snackbar component specifically — the brief, auto-dismissing message bar that appears at the bottom of the screen (e.g. 'Item deleted — Undo'). Because it disappears on its own after a short delay, generic control-steering can miss it entirely; this dedicated Module exists to interact with it reliably within its visible window.

bulletPoints: Snackbars are transient and auto-dismiss — a dedicated Module exists because generic steering can miss the window.

elements.title: When a mobile TestCase fails to connect or execute
items: Check the TMA console: is the device listed as Ready (not Busy or Offline)?
Query GET /api/devices directly on the TMA host — confirm connected:true, busy:false.
Verify the TCP values against documented format — TMAServer trailing slash, correct DeviceName, correct AppPackage/AppActivity or BundleID.
For Remote setups, confirm TMA was started with --rest-address, and that the port is open through any firewall.
Only after all of the above, investigate network/proxy causes.

elements.title: Common error patterns and what they usually mean
items: 'Could not create TMA session: Ensure that the requested device is connected' — despite the wording, this is very often a malformed TMAServer TCP (missing trailing slash), not an actual device problem.
Device visible in the OS/Finder/Explorer but invisible to TMA — almost always a missing prerequisite (USB debugging, Developer Mode, phone-data access) rather than a Tosca problem.
APK install fails with a certificate error — an old v1-only-signed APK on a newer Android version; re-sign with apksigner.
Scan succeeds but execution fails on the same connection — check the TMAServer trailing slash specifically, since the Scan wizard's Add connection dialog is more forgiving than execution.

bulletPoints: Diagnostic order: TMA console → REST API health check → TCP format check → firewall/network — in that order, not the reverse.
The most confusing error messages in mobile automation are the ones that name the wrong layer (a URL problem reported as a device problem).

examPitfalls.title: Assuming Android and iOS biometric Modules are interchangeable
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using the Android fingerprint Module against an iOS biometric prompt, or vice versa.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Android and iOS each require their own dedicated biometric Modules — they target platform-specific biometric APIs and are not interchangeable.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to simulate iOS biometric authentication without setting enrollment first
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Calling the iOS biometric authentication Module against a simulator that has never been configured as having biometrics enrolled.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Set iOS biometrics enrollment first — authentication cannot succeed against a target that isn't configured as enrolled.

examPitfalls.title: Letting Appium sessions linger on a shared device
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Finishing a TestCase without explicitly ending its Appium session, leaving the device unavailable to the next test or teammate until a timeout expires.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use End Appium Session explicitly to free the device promptly, especially in shared device-farm or CI settings.

examPitfalls.title: Interpreting connection error text literally
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reading 'Ensure that the requested device is connected' and spending time reconnecting or replacing the device.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: This exact message is frequently caused by a malformed TMAServer TCP (missing trailing slash), not an actual device problem — verify the TCP format before touching the device or network.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What must be configured before Use iOS biometric authentication can succeed?

options.text: The device's region and language settings.
Biometrics enrollment must be set via Set iOS biometrics enrollment.
The app must be reinstalled immediately beforehand.
LiveView must be enabled.

practiceQuiz.hint: Enrollment and authentication are two separate steps on iOS.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Set iOS biometrics enrollment configures whether the target is treated as having biometrics enrolled at all — a prerequisite before the authentication Module can succeed.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A brief 'Item deleted — Undo' bar appears at the bottom of an Android screen and auto-dismisses after a few seconds. Which Module is purpose-built for steering it?

options.text: Click On Screen
Android Snackbar
ME3.0 Hardware Button Operations
Send Text Input To Focused Control

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a named Android UI component, not a generic gesture.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Android Snackbar is a dedicated Module for the Android Snackbar component specifically — because it auto-dismisses quickly, generic steering can miss the window, which is why a dedicated Module exists.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A TestCase execution fails with 'Could not create TMA session: Ensure that the requested device is connected,' even though the same device connects fine during Mobile Scan. What should be checked first?

options.text: Whether the device's USB cable is faulty.
Whether the TMAServer TCP value ends with a trailing slash.
Whether the device needs a factory reset.
Whether the app under test has been updated.

practiceQuiz.hint: This exact wording is a known symptom of one specific configuration mistake.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This error message very often indicates a missing trailing slash on the TMAServer TCP — the Scan wizard's Add connection dialog tolerates its absence, while execution does not, which is exactly the symptom described.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a shared device-farm setting, what is the benefit of explicitly calling End Appium Session at the end of a TestCase?

options.text: It improves control identification accuracy.
It frees the device promptly for the next TestCase or teammate, instead of waiting for a session timeout.
It is required before Upload File to Mobile Device can run.
It disables biometric prompts for the next session.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what happens to a device left in a lingering session.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Ending the session explicitly frees the device promptly, which matters in shared device-farm or CI environments where the next TestCase or person is waiting — rather than leaving the device tied up until a timeout expires.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Following the recommended troubleshooting order, what should be checked immediately after confirming the device shows Ready in the TMA console?

options.text: Firewall and proxy configuration.
A direct GET /api/devices call to confirm connected/busy/statusReady values.
Whether the app under test needs to be reinstalled.
The device's biometric enrollment status.

practiceQuiz.hint: Confirm device health independently of the TMA console UI before checking anything network-related.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The recommended order checks the TMA console, then confirms device health directly via GET /api/devices, then verifies TCP format, and only then investigates network/firewall causes — each step rules out one layer before moving to the next.

quickRecap.value: ME3.0 Hardware Button Operations (Home/Back/volume/power) · ME3.0 Set Device Orientation (portrait/landscape).
Separate Modules per platform (Android fingerprint, iOS biometric) plus Perfecto-specific ones. iOS requires Set iOS biometrics enrollment before authentication.
Upload File to Mobile Device / Download File from Mobile Device — move data to/from the device filesystem.
Get Appium Session Id (for log correlation) · End Appium Session (free the device promptly, especially on shared farms).
Dedicated Module for the auto-dismissing Snackbar component — generic steering can miss its short visible window.
TMA console Ready → GET /api/devices → verify TCP format (trailing slash!) → Remote --rest-address/firewall → only then network/proxy.
'Ensure that the requested device is connected' is frequently a malformed TMAServer TCP, not a real device problem.
